t: You're standing in Addington Square, a Georgian and Regency garden square in Camberwell, in the London Borough of Southwark. It's named after Henry Addington, who later became Viscount Sidmouth. He was a Tory statesman who served as prime minister from 1801 to 1804, and before that as Speaker of the House of Commons from 1789 to 1801. The square takes its name from him, and the material I have doesn't say more about its history.
